## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

.github/workflows/opencode.yml
name: OpenCode
run-name: "OpenCode #${{ github.event.issue.number || inputs.issue_number }}${{ github.event.issue.title && format(' — {0}', github.event.issue.title) || '' }}"

on:
  issues:
    types: [opened]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue_number:
        description: Existing issue to run
        required: true
        type: string

permissions: {}

concurrency:
  group: opencode-issue-${{ github.repository }}-${{ github.event.issue.number || inputs.issue_number }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  prepare:
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' || (github.event.action == 'opened' && contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'OpenCode'))
    permissions:
      contents: write
      id-token: write
      issues: write
      actions: write
    uses: denaidark/OhMyGithub/.github/workflows/opencode-prepare.yml@73c5fea042dfb7c81e7f566fec2aa9c8ca8070ae
    with:
      runtime_ref: 73c5fea042dfb7c81e7f566fec2aa9c8ca8070ae

  opencode:
    needs: prepare
    if: needs.prepare.outputs.approved == 'true'
    permissions:
      contents: write
      id-token: write
      issues: write
      actions: read
      pull-requests: write
    uses: denaidark/OhMyGithub/.github/workflows/opencode-reusable.yml@73c5fea042dfb7c81e7f566fec2aa9c8ca8070ae
    with:
      runtime_ref: 73c5fea042dfb7c81e7f566fec2aa9c8ca8070ae
      issue_number: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.issue_number }}
      request: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.request }}
      issue_title: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.issue_title }}
      labels_json: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.labels_json }}
      sender: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.sender }}
      target_ref: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.target_ref }}
      target_sha: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.target_sha }}
    secrets:
      OPENCODE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENCODE_API_KEY }}
      OPENCODE_AUTH_JSON: ${{ secrets.OPENCODE_AUTH_JSON }}
      AGENTSWEB_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY: ${{ secrets.AGENTSWEB_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY }}
      OPENROUTER_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENROUTER_API_KEY }}
---agents
.agents/README.md
# Worker Agents Skills

This repository bundles the baseline skills installed by [Worker
Agents](https://github.com/agents-dev/workerAgents).

The bundled skills are available under [`skills/`](skills/):

- `mcp-duckgo` — imported from `aahl/skills@mcp-duckgo`.
- `image-search` — imported from `z0gsh1u/oh-my-writing-skill@image-search`.
- `gauntlet-loop` — imported from `robonuggets/gauntlet-loop@gauntlet-loop`.
- `load-sketchfab-threejs` — local asset inspection, normalization, and Three.js/PlayCanvas A/B viewer skill.
- `opencode-zen-completions` — use the OpenCode Zen chat completions API for implementation work.

The original upstream licenses are preserved in
[`third-party-licenses/`](third-party-licenses/).

# 🤯 OMG — Oh My GitHub ### 🚀 One Prompt In. A Full Game or App Out. 🚀 [![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-🔥%20works-brightgreen?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/actions) [![GitHub Issues](https://img.shields.io/github/issues/denaidark/OhMyGithub?style=for-the-badge&logo=github)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/issues) [![GitHub Actions](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub%20Actions-automated-2088FF?style=for-the-badge&logo=githubactions&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/actions) [![OpenCode](https://img.shields.io/badge/powered%20by-OpenCode-111111?style=for-the-badge)](https://opencode.ai/) ```text ╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗ ║ DESCRIBE IT → BUILD IT → TEST IT → PLAY IT ║ ║ ║ ║ One GitHub issue. One prompt. A complete project. ║ ╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝ ``` **No API keys to configure. No server to maintain. No local setup maze.**
--- ## 🤯 What Is OMG? > **Your GitHub issue becomes the product brief.** OMG (Oh My GitHub) is an automated GitHub Actions workflow for creating complete browser games and app projects from one natural-language prompt. Write what you want in an issue and add the `OpenCode` label. OpenCode checks out the project, uses the shared skills, builds the experience, runs tests, verifies the result, and publishes an immutable OmGithub project link from the finished commit. Yes, it creates the code. Yes, it runs the verification loop. Yes, it can expose the result in a temporary browser URL. ## 🧠 TL;DR 1. Open a GitHub issue. 2. Describe the game or app you want. 3. Add the `OpenCode` label to the issue. 4. Let GitHub Actions build, test, verify, and propose the result. ```text Your idea → GitHub issue → OpenCode → tests → immutable OmGithub project ``` ## ⚡ Quick Start Create an issue in your repository with a concrete request: ```text Build a neon asteroid game. Requirements: - Arrow-key movement - Score and restart button - Win and lose states - Responsive browser layout - Run tests and verify it in a browser ``` That is the whole user-facing workflow. GitHub Actions handles the runner, OpenCode handles implementation, and the workflow handles verification plus the immutable project commit. To run against an existing non-default branch, end the issue title with a `branch: ` directive. The directive selects the checkout and is removed before the issue body is sent to OpenCode: ```sh gh issue create \ --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub \ --title "Custom branch smoke test branch: codex/omgithub-site" \ --body "Build a tiny browser page." \ --label Goal \ --label OpenCode ``` The GitHub App validates the branch before dispatching. If the directive is absent, the repository default branch remains the target. ## 🌍 What Can You Build? | 🎯 Use case | ✨ Example | |---|---| | 🎮 Arcade games | Breakout, Space Invaders, Asteroids, Match-3 | | 🧩 Puzzle games | Word games, logic puzzles, card games | | 🏃 Interactive demos | Physics experiments, simulations, visual toys | | 📊 Dashboards | Filters, charts, status panels, analytics views | | 🛠️ Internal tools | Trackers, generators, small workflow apps | | 🌐 Landing pages | Product pages, portfolios, interactive showcases | | 🧪 Prototypes | Turn a product idea into a runnable proof of concept | | 📱 Browser apps | Responsive tools that work on desktop and mobile | ## 🧰 What Happens Automatically? > **The workflow is the product.** - 📥 Checks out your repository and the shared OpenCode skills. - 🏷️ Synchronizes `model/*` and `skill/*` labels. - 🧭 Reads issue labels to select the model and requested skills. - 🤖 Runs OpenCode against the current project. - 🧪 Runs a second verification prompt after implementation. - 🌐 Starts the app and checks the local runtime. - 🔗 Creates a temporary public preview URL when verification passes. - 🔀 Creates and pushes an `opencode/` branch. - 🕹️ Adds an `Open Project` link backed by the repository path, with full-commit links retained for compatibility. - 💬 Posts progress and access details back to the issue. - 🧹 Cleans up temporary tunnels and runner processes. ## 🏷️ Model and Skill Labels Labels let you control the workflow without editing YAML. ```text model/opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free skill/load-sketchfab-threejs skill/gauntlet-loop ``` The workflow validates the selected labels, passes them into OpenCode, and records the resolved model and skills in the run logs. Shared skills are discovered from: --- I want you to build a first-person shooter at the level of the most recent Call of Duty games. It should be utterly perfect, visually beautiful, with every single thing done at AAA quality—from textures to physics to anything you could think of. Fan out sub-agents and have sub-agents tackle each one individually so that the game is utterly perfect. Have a separate sub-agent check each item visually to ensure it looks triple A. That separate sub-agent should be a really harsh critic, and if it doesn't look triple A, keep iterating until it does. Don't stop until each sub-agent is utterly wowed with the quality when compared with the actual Call of Duty game. It should literally compare them side by side blind and say which one looks better. Do this in ThreeJS. Continue iterating until it's utterly perfect. messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable Monster Hunter World-inspired browser game where the player only uses Dual Blades, with high-quality visuals and responsive desktop/mobile controls.

## Requirements
- Build now without clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly at the end.
- Must be a complete playable game, not a prototype.
- User referenced Monster Hunter World and exclusively Dual Blades gameplay.

## Decisions
- Implemented as a static vanilla HTML/CSS/Canvas 2D game to avoid external runtime dependencies.
- Stylized 2.5D top-down forest hunt with procedural artwork, custom local fonts, and WebAudio audio.
- Original monster “Thornscale Tyrant” instead of copyrighted Monster Hunter assets.
- Core controls: WASD move, LMB/J slash combo, RMB/K Blade Dance, Shift/Space evade, Q Demon Mode, E potion, R sharpen, H guide, Esc/P pause.
- Added mobile joystick and touch action buttons.
- `willReadFrequently: true` on canvas contexts is required: without it, SwiftShader/Vulkan capture produced a blank canvas.
- Use `--disable-gpu` for reliable screenshots; GPU/Vulkan capture can be used now that `willReadFrequently` is set.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created full game shell: `index.html`, `style.css`, `game.js`.
- Implemented player movement, combos, Demon Mode, Blade Dance, dodge i-frames, potions, sharpening, stamina, health, sharpness, demon gauge, combo counter.
- Implemented monster AI: roar, charge, tail sweep, bite, acid volleys, enrage, stagger, limping, death.
- Implemented HUD, quest timer, monster bar, minimap, field guide, pause screen, victory/defeat screens, toasts, damage numbers, particles, screen shake/hitstop.
- Added local fonts in `assets/fonts`, but favicon is still missing (`assets/favicon.svg` 404).
- Added extensive visual upgrades: denser trees/ferns, richer ground shadows/roots/bones/litter, improved logs, monster scale texture, wings, mouth interior, horns, breath particles.
- Verified rendering using headed and headless Chromium; screenshots show UI and scene correctly with `willReadFrequently`.
- Temporary debugging globals exist: `window.__ironwood`, `window.__frames`, `window.__profile`; profiling instrumentation remains in `drawScene`.

### Active
- Visual polish iteration was underway: after latest monster/tree/fern/log/ground edits, no fresh screenshot has been captured or inspected.
- Need verify new staging trees, camera framing, monster detail, and performance.

### Blocked
- None.

## Next Move
1. Run `node -c game.js`, start/keep local server on `http://localhost:3002`, and capture fresh screenshots at 1440×900 around 2.5s and 6–8s.
2. Inspect composition: player/monster placement, monster clipping, new trees, ground contrast, banner readability.
3. Test combat interactions by simulating movement/attack/dodge and confirm damage, hits, stamina, and HUD updates.
4. Fix `assets/favicon.svg` 404 by creating the favicon.
5. Remove or minimize profiling/debug globals and instrumentation before finishing.
6. Test mobile viewport/touch layout and verify pause/guide/end-screen flows.
7. Update `README.md` with controls and brief project description, then report assumptions and completed features.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: full HUD, menus, mobile controls, script/CSS links.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/game.js`: entire game engine, rendering, AI, combat, UI, audio; latest visual edits applied.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/style.css`: all HUD/menu/responsive styling and animations.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/assets/fonts/`: local Cinzel and Barlow Condensed font files.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/screenshots/`: generated verification screenshots (`software.png`, `scene6.png`, `vulkan.png`, etc.).
- `/tmp/opencode/shot2.mjs`: reusable Playwright screenshot script using headless Chromium with `--disable-gpu`.
- `/tmp/opencode/vulkantest.mjs`: confirms GPU/Vulkan screenshot works with `willReadFrequently`.
- `/tmp/opencode/perf.mjs`: profiling script for frame counts and render-section timings.

## Important Context
- Local static server currently likely running on port 3002 via `python3 -m http.server 3002 --bind 0.0.0.0`.
- `playwright-cli` screenshots timed out with GPU flags; direct Playwright scripts work, especially with `--disable-gpu`.
- Canvas contexts are created with `{ alpha: false, willReadFrequently: true }`; offscreen ground context also uses `willReadFrequently`.
- Base zoom changed to `clamp(Math.min(W / 1180, H / 700), 0.92, 1.34)`.
- Spawn positions now: player `x=-220,z=130`, monster `x=300,z=-20`; initial camera `-76,58`.
- Sprite projection uses `Y_SCALE = 0.62`; world arena radii `1450×950`.
- Performance under SwiftShader is roughly 12–14 fps, but measured JS render time is only ~2.5ms/frame; most time is software compositing.
- Accessibility/UI state: quest banner auto-fades; hint chip shows tutorial text; game starts immediately with no blocking start menu.

# The Ironwood Hunt

A complete, playable dual-blades monster hunt for the browser. It is a stylized top-down forest arena inspired by the pacing and weapon fantasy of *Monster Hunter*, built entirely with HTML, CSS, Canvas 2D, and Web Audio. No build step or external runtime is required.

The game is an original work: the monster, hunter, forest, UI, artwork, and audio are procedural or hand-authored for this project. It does not use Capcom assets.

## Play

```bash
python3 -m http.server 3002 --bind 0.0.0.0
```

Open `http://localhost:3002`.

The game starts immediately. A local static server is recommended because the custom fonts are loaded as local assets.

## Controls

| Action | Desktop | Touch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Move | `WASD` / arrow keys | Virtual joystick |
| Dual slash combo | Left click / `J` / `F` | **Slash** |
| Blade Dance | Right click / `K` | **Dance** |
| Evade with i-frames | `Shift` / `Space` | **Evade** |
| Demon Mode | `Q` | **Demon** |
| Mega Potion | `E` | **Potion** |
| Sharpen | `R` | **Hone** |
| Field guide | `H` | Pause → Field guide |
| Pause | `Esc` / `P` | Pause button |
| Toggle sound | Speaker button | Speaker button |

## Hunt

- **Thornscale Tyrant** has a full attack loop: roar, charge, tail sweep, bite, acid volleys, enrage, stagger, wounded/limping state, and death.
- The hunter manages health, stamina, sharpness, potions, combo timing, Demon Mode drain, and dodge invulnerability.
- Red ground telegraphs mark heavy attacks. Dodge through them for i-frames.
- Keep blades sharp. White sharpness deals more damage; low sharpness cuts damage significantly.
- The 12-minute quest timer, monster health bar, minimap, HUD, field guide, pause menu, victory screen, defeat screen, and retry flow are all implemented.
- Rendering includes procedural ground, foliage, water, atmospheric effects, hit particles, damage numbers, screen shake, hit-stop, and a dynamic camera.

## Project Files

- `index.html` — game shell, HUD, menus, touch controls.
- `style.css` — visual design, responsive layout, animations, mobile controls.
- `game.js` — engine, combat, monster AI, rendering, audio, UI state.
- `assets/fonts/` — local Cinzel and Barlow Condensed fonts.
- `assets/favicon.svg` — site icon.

## Notes

- Desktop and mobile layouts are supported, including a dedicated touch control set with Hone and pause access.
- The game is tuned for a modern browser with Canvas 2D and Web Audio support.
- For the most reliable headless capture, use Chromium with `--disable-gpu`; the canvas context uses `willReadFrequently` so software capture reads the scene correctly.

A finished, playable Dual Blades hunt with:

- Four-hit slash combo, Blade Dance, dodge i-frames, Demon Mode, potions, sharpening, stamina, sharpness, and combo chaining.
- Full monster AI: roar, charge, tail sweep, bite, acid volleys, enrage, stagger, wounded/limping state, and death.
- Quest timer, monster health, minimap, HUD, field guide, pause menu, victory/defeat screens, and retry flow.
- Procedural forest artwork, weather/atmosphere, hit particles, damage numbers, screen shake, hit-stop, dynamic camera, and Web Audio sound.
- Responsive desktop and mobile layouts, including joystick, touch actions, Hone, and a mobile pause button.

## Run

```bash
python3 -m http.server 3002 --bind 0.0.0.0
```

Open `http://localhost:3002`.

## Controls

- Move: `WASD` / arrows
- Slash: LMB / `J`
- Blade Dance: RMB / `K`
- Evade: `Shift` / `Space`
- Demon Mode: `Q`
- Potion: `E`
- Sharpen: `R`
- Guide: `H`
- Pause: `Esc` / `P`

Touch controls mirror these actions.

Verified desktop and mobile layouts, combat hits, dance damage, potions, sharpening, touch controls, pause/guide flow, and both victory and defeat screens with no browser console errors. `README.md`, favicon, local fonts, and responsive styling are included.

## Assumptions

- Used an original monster and forest rather than copyrighted Monster Hunter assets.
- Focused on one polished, replayable hunt rather than a larger campaign/crafting hub.
- Built as a dependency-free static HTML/CSS/Canvas game, tuned for modern desktop and mobile browsers.
